title: Securing React Applications
description: Apply XSS and CSRF defenses in React components and routing.

data.text: React provides some built-in safety, but you still need to be intentional about handling user input and external data.
Never pass untrusted content to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. If you must render HTML, sanitize it first with a library like DOMPurify.

items: Validate input length and type before sending
Escape user-generated content before inserting into the DOM
Use URL parsing instead of string concatenation for links
Avoid inline event handlers in dynamically generated HTML

data.text: SPAs often forget CSRF tokens on navigation. Use a global fetch wrapper or Axios interceptor to ensure every state-changing request includes the token.

data.title: Third-Party Scripts
data.text: Be careful with analytics or ads. Use Subresource Integrity (SRI) and CSP to limit damage if a third-party script is compromised.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use DOMPurify for any HTML sanitization
data.takeaway: With XSS and CSRF covered, we can now harden the API itself.
